thread:
maria: heads up — apiserver 503 spike in eu-west1 around 10:05 UTC, controller-manager leader flips happening. auth cache evictions + watch reconnects.
aj: looking. grabbing logs.
devon: saw a KMS rotation job at ~10:03, could have invalidated signing keys triggering SAR failures.
maria: logs show "SubjectAccessReview failed: user not found" and aggregator proxies returning 503s.
kai: metrics: apiserver latency -> 4x, etcd write_iops up, watch backlog growing on controller-manager.
olivia: also seeing a GPU attach storm from training-jobs — many pods in Pending hammering attach webhooks to rtx-pools.
aj: running quick grep:
```
kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-apiserver-eu-west1 | grep -E "SubjectAccessReview|etcd request"
```
devon: starting a rolling restart of kube-aggregator. suggestion: bump auth-cache TTL 30s -> 120s to reduce SAR pressure.
maria: oncall plan:
  1) increase auth-cache TTL to 120s
  2) throttle gpu-provisioning webhook attach parallelism
  3) prepare controller-manager failover if leader keeps flipping
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20240312-EUW1-APISERVER-503 :warning:
deploy-bot: proposed patch applied in dry-run: kube-apiserver.authCacheTTL=120s — awaiting go-ahead.
kai: also propose reducing provisioner attach_parallelism: 10 -> 3 in /etc/provisioner/config
olivia: reducing attach_parallelism now (rolling config reload).
aj: after throttling, etcd write ops down ~45%, apiserver 503s dropped, controller-manager leader stable :thumbsup:
maria: leaving auth-cache TTL=120s for 2h and monitoring. follow-ups: add circuit-breaker to provisioner for etcd latency >200ms and add test for KMS rotation impact.
devon: opened ENG-3456 for provisioner circuit-breaker and runbook update.
maria: thanks everyone — will draft a short postmortem and schedule a retro. :pray:
